newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso ends down on stk mkt outflows.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso ends down on stk mkt outflows.

text.p: The Philippine peso fell to 26.368 at the close on Monday from 26.365 as it was pulled down by the outflow of overseas funds from the domestic stock market, traders said.
The Philippine Stock Exchange lost on Tuesday 2.28 percent, or 69.63 points on the main index due to concerns over the state of property and banking sectors.
The day's average, however, showed a stronger peso at 26.365 from 26.367 because banks had been selling their dollars early in the day for pesos that earn the higher interest rate.
Volume narrowed to $127.1 million from $236.7 million.
But the peso slowly lost ground when the Central Bank started calling banks in the morning to buy dollars.
A trader estimated the Central Bank bought about $35 million at 26.363 to replenish some of the dollars it sold last Friday.
"The market remains very cautious," a dealer said. Banks still want to hold on to the dollar since the stock market had been on a downtrend and domestic interest rates are still low.
